title: "Figure (number pending) — the density half of the design plane: which approximation is closer to the truth, and along which axis of the family"

<!--
NUMBER PENDING. The slot is not decided. The argument for putting it BEFORE Figure 4 is that it
shows the ranking a likelihood comparison gives, so that Figure 4's headline then refutes something
the reader has just been shown rather than asserting it cold. The argument for a supplement is page
budget. Neither is settled here.

THE QUANTITY, and it is the axis Figure 4 does not have. Every panel is a DIFFERENCE of summed
log-likelihoods between two members, both evaluated at theta_sim, the simulation truth, so

    E[log p_A] - E[log p_B] = KL(true || p_B) - KL(true || p_A),

a difference of Kullback-Leibler divergence rates, positive when the member with more machinery is
the closer density. There is no estimator in it. Figure 4 measures what a member's REPORT gets
wrong, in the first moment and in the second; this page measures what its DENSITY gets wrong, which
is the property a model comparison would actually rank on.

WHY THETA_SIM AND NOT THETA_POOL, the opposite anchor from Figure 4's distortion half. The
comparison means nothing unless every member is evaluated at the SAME parameter. At each member's
own optimum the difference would mix density quality with parameter fitting and would penalise the
two least-squares arms for holding the unitary current and the noise level fixed.

THE UNIT IS NATS PER RECORDING AND IT IS NOT DIVIDED BY THE SAMPLE COUNT. Every recording on this
grid is 10 tau long in every cell, verified against Sum_r2_std, whose null is the interval count
10/Delta_tilde and which reads 999.5 / 499.8 / 199.9 against 1000 / 500 / 200. So the emitted SUM is
already a quantity per unit time and there is no varying recording length to correct for. Dividing
by the interval count multiplies by Delta_tilde/10, a hundredfold ramp along the horizontal axis
that is nothing but the sample count. Measured both ways 2026-08-12, as the spread of the median
contrast along the interval axis: raw is flatter in EIGHT of the nine contrasts, six of them by two
orders of magnitude (ILSE-LSE 202x raw against 20200x per sample). The exception is R-NR, 14.7x raw
against 8.75x per sample, and it is marginal. The `logl-normalisation` chunk prints the whole
comparison rather than asking anyone to take this on trust.

THE CONTRASTS ARE THE EDGES OF THE FAMILY'S LATTICE, always in the direction MORE MACHINERY minus
LESS, so positive always means the extra step bought density and no panel is read backwards. Under
that convention MR - R and VR - R come out negative, and that IS the finding rather than a sign to
apologise for. They are grouped by WHICH AXIS OF THE FAMILY the step moves, and the grouping is the
whole point of the page: the averaging block is nearly blank and the recursion block is saturated,
which a reader gets before reading a single number. The two four-member squares are drawn with all
their edges, which makes two of them redundant by construction, (ILSE-LSE) + (INR-ILSE) =
(NR-LSE) + (INR-NR) exactly. That redundancy is kept: it is a visible closure check and it costs two
narrow columns.

THE SCALE REACHES BELOW ONE NAT AND STOPS AT 0.1, which is where the measurement says it has to
stop. Each member is scored on its OWN ensemble of 10,000 simulated recordings, so a contrast is a
difference of two INDEPENDENT means with standard error sqrt(v_A/n_A + v_B/n_B) from the emitted
per-recording variance. That floor is NOT uniform over a panel: the summed log-likelihood's spread
grows as the square root of the interval count, so 2 SE runs 0.64 nats at Delta_tilde = 0.01 and
0.064 at Delta_tilde = 1, a factor of ten across the horizontal axis of every panel. Measured by
band, the fraction of cells that clear their own floor: under 0.03 nats, NONE of 181; 0.03 to 0.1,
5 per cent; 0.1 to 0.3, 19 per cent; 0.3 to 1, 73 per cent; 1 to 3, 94 per cent. A band at 0.03
would therefore paint sampling noise in every cell it touched and is not drawn. 0.1 is drawn,
because the smallest floor anywhere on the grid is 0.056 and a cell at the coarse end can earn it.

WHICH IT HAS TO EARN, PER CELL. A cell whose difference is inside its own +-2 SE is set to exactly
zero and renders white, so a sub-nat band appears only where the floor is below it. The figure
therefore shows its own resolution rather than declaring it, and that is why the sub-nat structure
fades leftward in every panel: the fine end of a panel cannot resolve a tenth of a nat and says so
by going white. A white iso-line at the resolution boundary was tried and dropped, because after
the collapse it traces the boundary of the field it sits on, which the layout's own note says reads
as an error.

BELOW THE PER-CELL FLOOR THERE IS STILL SIGNAL, and it is pooled rather than drawn. The
`sub-nat-signal` chunk takes the inverse-variance weighted mean of the whole sub-1 region per
contrast: every one of the nine is many standard errors from zero, +0.218 for IR - R, +0.110 for
ILSE - LSE, -0.497 for NR - LSE and -0.455 for INR - ILSE. So the sub-nat region is not empty, it
is merely below what one cell of this ensemble can see, and the two signs are worth the sentence:
averaging gains a tenth to a fifth of a nat systematically, and modelling the gating variance
COSTS about half a nat once the instrumental noise dominates.

GEOMETRY IS THE SHARED RENDERER'S, not this notebook's. fig4_render with outer = "param" puts the
axis group on the outer column level and the contrast on the inner one, which is structurally the
same layout as figure_4_S4.Rmd's parameter blocks with members inside them. That buys the isotropy
constraint (one decade of interval and one decade of noise the same physical distance), the row
heights proportional to the noise span each channel count reaches, the boxed strips, the single x
row and the colour bar, all identical to the rest of the set. The one thing it costs is that ALGOS
has to be re-pointed at the contrasts AFTER figure_4_common.R has built GRID_BY_ALGO from the real
members, so the detected grid and the row heights stay derived from runs on disk; the contrast keys
inherit the grid of their more expensive member, which is the cell set the inner join produces
anyway.

GREY is the renderer's own terminal band, plus Figure 4's rule for the ill-conditioned corner
(kappa > 3e4), read from Figure 4's own cell scalars so the two pages grey together.

THE EXTRACTION HAS A TRAP, documented in figure_4_logL_data.R. Each (member, cell, interval) emits
six rows with statistic == "mean": the point estimate at probit == "mean" and five
percentile-bootstrap rows at probit == "quantile". They differ by about 0.05% of the sum, which on a
sum of -7000 nats is +-4 nats, larger than several of the contrasts this page exists to measure.
Both conditions are required.
-->

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
```

```{r common, include=FALSE}
# STEP 1. Source the shared machinery with the REAL member roster, so GRID_BY_ALGO, YLIM, cells and
# nch_noise_span are all derived from runs that exist on disk. FIG4_DATA_DIRS is figure_4.Rmd:331
# verbatim: five directories, first hit wins. NOT a glob over ../data, which also turns up 82b956f
# for IR, MR and R and is not on the figure's path.
FIG4_ALGOS     <- c("nonlinearsqr_g", "nonlinearsqr", "macro_NR", "macro_INR",
                    "macro_R", "macro_MR", "macro_VR", "macro_IR")
FIG4_ALGO_LAB  <- c(nonlinearsqr_g = "LSE", nonlinearsqr = "ILSE", macro_NR = "NR",
                    macro_INR = "INR", macro_R = "R", macro_MR = "MR",
                    macro_VR = "VR", macro_IR = "IR")
FIG4_DATA_DIRS <- c("../data/1c2ae6f", "../data/87889e6", "../data/0ffbda7", "../data/1f7138b",
                    "../data/a202e03")
MEMBERS <- FIG4_ALGOS

# the outer column level is the axis of the family the step moves; labels are parsed as plotmath,
# so they are quoted strings
# the UNION of both sides' groups, in reading order. half() drops the ones a side has no data for,
# so side A keeps the first four and side B the last three with no bookkeeping here.
# ORDER on side A: the gating variance first, then the recursion, then the averaging, then the
# partial rung that conditions on one endpoint instead of two. That is the order the argument runs
# in, and it is not the order the lattice was written in: it puts the two steps that move the
# density most next to each other and leaves the two that barely move it at the end, so the reader
# meets the result before the null.
FIG4_PARS   <- c("gvar", "rec", "avg", "part", "lsq", "open", "recur")
FIG4_PSHORT <- c(avg  = "'averaging'", gvar = "'gating variance'", rec = "'recursion'",
                 part = "'one endpoint'",
                 lsq  = "'least squares'", open = "'open loop'", recur = "'recursive rungs'")

source("figure_4_common.R")
source("figure_4_logL_data.R")

logl   <- fig4_logL_build()
logl$m <- FIG4_ALGO_LAB[logl$algo]
```

```{r contrasts}
# TWO SIDES, ONE MEASUREMENT. (A) the EDGES of the family's lattice, one step at a time, grouped by
# which axis the step moves: what does each axis buy. (B) every member against IR, grouped by
# family: how far behind is each member. Neither subsumes the other -- an edge can buy a lot without
# the member that took it being any good, and a ranking says nothing about which step is
# responsible -- and they share a quantity, a unit and a scale, so they share a colour bar.
CONTRASTS <- tibble::tribble(
  ~hi,    ~lo,    ~param, ~side,
  "ILSE", "LSE",  "avg",   1,
  "INR",  "NR",   "avg",   1,
  "IR",   "R",    "avg",   1,
  "NR",   "LSE",  "gvar",  1,
  "INR",  "ILSE", "gvar",  1,
  "R",    "NR",   "rec",   1,
  "IR",   "INR",  "rec",   1,
  "MR",   "R",    "part",  1,
  "VR",   "R",    "part",  1,
  # cheapest first inside every group, which is the cost ladder R -> MR -> VR -> IR, NOT the order
  # the contrasts were first written in
  "IR",   "LSE",  "lsq",   2,
  "IR",   "ILSE", "lsq",   2,
  "IR",   "NR",   "open",  2,
  "IR",   "INR",  "open",  2,
  "IR",   "R",    "recur", 2,
  "IR",   "MR",   "recur", 2,
  "IR",   "VR",   "recur", 2)
# the key has to distinguish IR-R on side B from the IR-R edge on side A, which are the same
# difference read for two different reasons and must not collide in ALGOS
CONTRASTS$algo <- sprintf("%s_%s_%d", CONTRASTS$hi, CONTRASTS$lo, CONTRASTS$side)
# THE COLUMN LABEL IS THE SUBTRACTION, ON TWO LINES. At sixteen columns "ILSE - LSE" on one line
# does not fit the 1.33 mm cell and arrived clipped ("SE - LS"). Stacking it as atop() fits, and it
# beats naming one member of the pair and leaving the group header to imply the other: the reader
# sees WHICH difference the panel is without reconstructing it. Minuend on top, subtrahend below, so
# every column reads the same way and side B's seven columns all repeat IR over the member it is
# measured against. The layout's inner label passes an expression through unquoted; a plain token
# still gets quoted, which is what every other figure in the set has.
CONTRASTS$lab  <- sprintf("%s\n- %s", CONTRASTS$hi, CONTRASTS$lo)
CONTRASTS$pair <- sprintf("%s - %s", CONTRASTS$hi, CONTRASTS$lo)
KEY_OF_MEMBER  <- setNames(names(FIG4_ALGO_LAB), FIG4_ALGO_LAB)

pair <- function(i) {
  cols <- c("Num_ch", "noise", "interval_in_tau", "logL", "var_logL", "n_sim")
  a <- dplyr::filter(logl, m == CONTRASTS$hi[i])[, cols]
  b <- dplyr::filter(logl, m == CONTRASTS$lo[i])[, cols]
  dplyr::inner_join(a, b, by = c("Num_ch", "noise", "interval_in_tau"),
                    suffix = c(".a", ".b")) %>%
    dplyr::transmute(Num_ch, noise, interval_in_tau,
                     d  = logL.a - logL.b,
                     se = sqrt(var_logL.a / n_sim.a + var_logL.b / n_sim.b),
                     algo = CONTRASTS$algo[i], param = CONTRASTS$param[i],
                     side = CONTRASTS$side[i], hi = CONTRASTS$hi[i], lo = CONTRASTS$lo[i])
}
CD <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(CONTRASTS)), pair)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(Num_ch %in% NCHS) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(lx = log10(interval_in_tau), ly = log10(as.numeric(noise)),
                noise = as.character(noise),
                # 1 is where the cell resolves its OWN difference
                z2 = abs(d) / (2 * se))

# Figure 4's ill-conditioned corner, joined on whichever member of the pair is the one that runs
# away: the more expensive one on side A, the cheaper one on side B, where IR is never it.
kap <- .fig4_src$scal %>% dplyr::filter(param == "kappa") %>%
  dplyr::transmute(kkey = algo, Num_ch, noise = as.character(noise), interval_in_tau, kappa = v)
CD <- CD %>%
  dplyr::mutate(kkey = KEY_OF_MEMBER[ifelse(side == 1, hi, lo)]) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(kap, by = c("kkey", "Num_ch", "noise", "interval_in_tau"))

# Re-point the roster at the contrasts, now that the grid is built from the real members. Each key
# inherits the detected grid of the member that owns its cell set.
for (i in seq_len(nrow(CONTRASTS)))
  GRID_BY_ALGO[[CONTRASTS$algo[i]]] <-
    GRID_BY_ALGO[[KEY_OF_MEMBER[[if (CONTRASTS$side[i] == 1) CONTRASTS$hi[i] else CONTRASTS$lo[i]]]]]
ALGOS    <- CONTRASTS$algo
ALGO_LAB <- setNames(CONTRASTS$lab, CONTRASTS$algo)
EXCLUDE_ROWS <- tidyr::expand_grid(algo = CONTRASTS$algo, param = FIG4_PARS) %>%
  dplyr::anti_join(CONTRASTS[, c("algo", "param")], by = c("algo", "param"))

source("figure_4_layout.R")

# THE OUTPUT DEVICE, and it is a one-line shadow rather than an edit to anything shared.
# fig4_render ends in `ggsave(out, g, width = 7.4, height = H)` with no device argument, so a .pdf
# goes out through the base pdf() device, which degrades every glyph outside its encoding to a full
# stop: a delta arrives as "." whether it is written literally, as a \u0394 escape, or built with
# intToUtf8, and it did. No PDF converter recovers it -- Ghostscript, which is what embedFonts()
# drives, can embed and subset fonts but cannot put back a character the device never drew. The fix
# has to happen at write time, and cairo_pdf writes Unicode.
# Defining ggsave HERE, after the source, is enough: fig4_render resolves the name at call time and
# finds this one first. figure_4_layout.R is untouched and every other notebook in the set keeps the
# classic device it has always used.
ggsave <- function(...) ggplot2::ggsave(..., device = cairo_pdf)
```

```{r scale}
# SIGNED DECADES ABOUT ZERO, reaching down to 0.1 nats. 3 and 100 are band EDGES, so the two criteria
# are named by the bar where they sit and the line key needs no swatch, which is Figure 4's device.
# The floor at 0.1 is where the per-cell resolution ends: the smallest 2 SE anywhere on the grid is
# 0.056, so a band at 0.03 could not be earned by any cell and is not drawn.
LOGL_BRK <- c(-3300, -1000, -300, -100, -30, -10, -3, -1, -0.3, -0.1,
              0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30, 100, 300, 1000, 3300)
SCALE_LOGL <- list(brk = LOGL_BRK, pal = bandcols(LOGL_BRK),
                   lab = c("", formatC(LOGL_BRK[-c(1, length(LOGL_BRK))], format = "g"), ""),
                   sol = c(-3, 3), dsh = c(-100, 100),
                   title = "\u0394 log-likelihood,\nin nats per recording of 10 \u03c4")

# THE SUB-NAT BANDS ARE DRAWN ONLY WHERE THE CELL EARNS THEM. A cell whose difference is inside its
# own +-2 SE is set to exactly zero and renders white, so a band at 0.1 nats can only appear where
# 2 SE is below 0.1, which happens at the coarse end of a panel and never at the fine end. The
# figure therefore shows its own resolution instead of needing a line to declare it, and it is why
# the sub-nat structure fades leftward in every panel. NOT a white iso-line on top: the layout's own
# note says a line tracing the boundary of the field it sits on reads as an error, and after the
# collapse that is exactly what it would trace.
CD$dconf <- ifelse(CD$z2 > 1, CD$d, 0)

# ONE SCALE, so the two sides share one bar spanning the whole width, which is what the renderer
# does for commensurable quantities and what makes the comparison between the halves legitimate.
SIDES <- list(
  list(lab = "\u0394 log-likelihood: each step of the ladder, one at a time", letter = "A",
       data = dplyr::filter(CD, side == 1), zf = function(x) x$dconf, scale = SCALE_LOGL),
  list(lab = "\u0394 log-likelihood: every member against IR", letter = "B",
       data = dplyr::filter(CD, side == 2), zf = function(x) x$dconf, scale = SCALE_LOGL))

# NO SILENT CAPS.
cat(sprintf("collapsed to zero as unresolved: %d of %d cells (%d of them above 1 nat)\n",
            sum(CD$z2 <= 1), nrow(CD), sum(CD$z2 <= 1 & abs(CD$d) > 1)))
cat(sprintf("clamped into the end band: %d cells; of those %d are ill-conditioned (kappa > 3e4)\n",
            sum(CD$dconf < min(LOGL_BRK) | CD$dconf > max(LOGL_BRK)),
            sum((CD$dconf < min(LOGL_BRK) | CD$dconf > max(LOGL_BRK)) &
                is.finite(CD$kappa) & CD$kappa > 3e4)))
cat(sprintf("cells on side B where a cheaper member beats IR by more than 3 nats: %d of %d\n",
            sum(CD$d[CD$side == 2] < -3), sum(CD$side == 2)))
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7.39, fig.height = 6.40}
# PER_ROW for SIXTEEN columns, which is the column count the harness has already solved: the note in
# figure_4_layout.R gives 16 -> 0.204 (x 0.1817, y 0.1807, 99.5 per cent), measured on this same
# layout. Verified here rather than assumed, with
#   python3 tmp/measure_fig4.py <pdf>
# against a target of 100 per cent isotropy.
# WHY THE TWO SIDES ARE ONE FIGURE AND NOT TWO. Under the isotropy constraint the height goes as the
# summed noise decades over the COLUMN COUNT, so putting the two sets side by side makes the page
# SHORTER, not longer: nine columns alone came to 11.1 in and seven alone to 14.0, against 9.6 in of
# usable text height measured off the built manuscript, so neither fitted a page with a caption.
# Sixteen columns bring it to about 6.4 in and leave room for one. The merge is not a compromise
# forced by the page; it is what the geometry rewards, and the two sets share a quantity, a unit and
# a scale, so they also share a colour bar.
# 0.204 is the harness's solved value for sixteen columns with a ONE-line inner strip. The stacked
# two-line label eats vertical space inside the map row and took that render to 95.9 per cent, so it
# is re-solved, and re-solved AGAIN after the device changed: cairo_pdf sets text with slightly
# different metrics from the base pdf device, so the fixed rows take different inches and a knob
# calibrated under one is wrong under the other. 0.208 measured 99.8 on the base device and 99.0 on
# cairo; under cairo 0.210 and 0.212 give 100.1 and 101.2.
PER_ROW_LOGL <- if (exists("PER_ROW_OVERRIDE")) PER_ROW_OVERRIDE else 0.210
fig4_render(SIDES, per_row = PER_ROW_LOGL, out = "Figure_4_logL.pdf",
            se_lines = FALSE, key = FALSE, outer = "param", drawn_axis = TRUE)
```

```{r logl-normalisation}
# THE NORMALISATION, measured rather than argued, because the header asserts it. For each contrast,
# the spread of the median along the interval axis under the two candidate units. Flat is better: a
# trend one unit has and the other does not is a trend that unit manufactured, since nothing about
# the members changes between the two columns. The blown corner is dropped first, NR's omitted N*ms
# term reaching 5.2e6 nats there and owning every median it touches.
flat <- function(x) { v <- abs(x); max(v) / max(min(v), 1e-12) }
CD %>% dplyr::filter(!(Num_ch >= 1000 & interval_in_tau >= 0.5 & abs(d) > 1000)) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(CONTRASTS[, c("algo", "pair")], by = "algo") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(pair, interval_in_tau) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(raw = median(d), per = median(d * interval_in_tau / 10), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(pair) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(`raw (nats per recording)` = flat(raw),
                   `per interval`             = flat(per), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~signif(., 3))) %>% as.data.frame() %>% print()
```

```{r sub-nat-signal}
# THE SUB-NAT REGION, which the scale now reaches into and which therefore has to be defended.
# TWO questions. First, where is the per-cell floor: 2 SE by band of |difference|, and what fraction
# of cells in each band clear their own floor. Second, is there systematic structure BELOW that
# floor: the inverse-variance weighted mean of the sub-1 region against its own standard error, so
# a |z| far from zero says the field is coherent even where no single cell is.
cat("=== per-cell resolution floor, 2 SE in nats ===\n")
print(signif(quantile(2 * CD$se, c(0, .25, .5, .75, .95, 1)), 3))
cat("\n=== 2 SE by sampling interval (it grows as the square root of the interval count) ===\n")
CD %>% dplyr::group_by(interval_in_tau) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(`2 SE` = signif(median(2 * se), 2), .groups = "drop") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print()
cat("\n=== resolved cells by band of |difference| ===\n")
CD %>% dplyr::mutate(band = cut(abs(d), c(0, .03, .1, .3, 1, 3, Inf),
                                labels = c("<0.03", "0.03-0.1", "0.1-0.3", "0.3-1", "1-3", ">3"))) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(band) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(cells = dplyr::n(), resolved = sum(z2 > 1),
                   fraction = signif(mean(z2 > 1), 2), .groups = "drop") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print()
cat("\n=== systematic signal in the sub-1 region: inverse-variance weighted mean and its z ===\n")
CD %>% dplyr::filter(abs(d) < 1) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(CONTRASTS[, c("algo", "param", "pair")], by = c("algo", "param")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(param, pair) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(cells = dplyr::n(),
                   `weighted mean` = sum(d / se^2) / sum(1 / se^2),
                   z = (sum(d / se^2) / sum(1 / se^2)) * sqrt(sum(1 / se^2)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~signif(., 3))) %>% as.data.frame() %>% print()
```

```{r what-the-likelihood-ranks}
# WHAT THE LIKELIHOOD RANKS, the reading the page exists for and the number the manuscript would
# quote. Fraction of cells where the more expensive member gains, or loses, more than the solid
# criterion of 3 nats over one recording.
CD %>% dplyr::left_join(CONTRASTS[, c("algo", "param", "pair")], by = c("algo", "param")) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(param, pair) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(cells = dplyr::n(),
                   `gains > 3 nats` = mean(d >  3),
                   `loses > 3 nats` = mean(d < -3),
                   median = median(d), `worst loss` = min(d), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~signif(., 3))) %>% as.data.frame() %>% print()

cat("\n=== median gain by channel count, nats per recording ===\n")
CD %>% dplyr::filter(!(Num_ch >= 1000 & interval_in_tau >= 0.5 & abs(d) > 1000)) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(CONTRASTS[, c("algo", "pair")], by = "algo") %>%
  dplyr::group_by(pair, Num_ch) %>% dplyr::summarise(v = median(d), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Num_ch, values_from = v) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~signif(., 3))) %>% as.data.frame() %>% print()

cat("\n=== median gain by instrumental noise at N_ch = 100, nats per recording ===\n")
CD %>% dplyr::filter(Num_ch == 100) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(CONTRASTS[, c("algo", "pair")], by = "algo") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(S = dimensionless_noise(as.numeric(noise))) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(pair, S) %>% dplyr::summarise(v = median(d), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = S, values_from = v) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(where(is.numeric), ~signif(., 3))) %>% as.data.frame() %>% print()
```
